suggestions.assertion: Daily Handoff is at most 12,000 characters
suggestions.reason: This is the only assertion that penalises length while 16 others reward content presence, so the scoring gradient actively pushes the skill toward bloat — the run scored 17/18 on content and still produced a document 4.3x the size of the transcript it replaces. Consider a second size-shaped assertion that bites on structure rather than raw count, e.g. 'no single fact (the legacy freeze, AUTH-214, the TTL placeholder) is restated in more than two sections' — the legacy freeze appears 4 times, the TTL placeholder 5 times, and sections 10-11 largely re-serialise sections 2-9.

suggestions.assertion: No section consists solely of 'N/A', 'None', or placeholder filler - unfilled sections are deleted outright
suggestions.reason: Ambiguous scope: it says 'section' but the realistic failure mode is field-level filler inside a section. This output has 'Required Inputs: None' and 'Blocking Conditions: None' inside section 9 — I passed it on the section reading, but a different grader could fail it. Pin the granularity explicitly (e.g. 'no heading OR labelled field is left with only N/A/None/TBD') so the verdict is deterministic.

No assertion checks that the handoff is written into the project repo (docs/handoffs/) rather than only into outputs/. Assertion 1 says 'under docs/handoffs/' but a run that produced only an outputs/ copy could plausibly be argued through. Worth stating that the file must exist at <project>/docs/handoffs/.

Nothing rewards the repo-verified findings that made this handoff genuinely more useful than the transcript — vitest declared in the test script but missing from dependencies, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md now stale on session storage, and the CSRF obligation implied by the cookie decision. These are the highest-value outputs of the run and are currently invisible to the score. An assertion like 'identifies at least one resumption blocker not stated in the transcript (e.g. stale ARCHITECTURE.md, missing vitest dependency)' would be discriminating.

suggestions.assertion: Next action is executable: names specific file paths or commands
suggestions.reason: Passable by any output containing a shell command. What made this one good is that the next action is the *right* one (commit before anything else, since the whole session is untracked). Consider asserting the first action addresses the uncommitted working tree, which is the actual highest-risk item in the ground truth.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set covers ground-truth fidelity thoroughly and caught the real regression — content quality is high (17/18) but the 12,000-char cap was missed by 26% at 15,148 characters. The main weakness is the reward gradient: one length assertion against sixteen presence assertions incentivises exactly the redundancy seen here. Adding a redundancy/structure assertion and one rewarding repo-derived findings would make the suite discriminate between 'complete' and 'complete and tight'.
